title.narrative: Provision of integrated Early Recovery and Protection Assistance to vulnerable populations in Aleppo and Daara Governorates

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed multi-sectoral project will contribute to ensure the most vulnerable populations in underserved locations affected by conflict, displacement, and natural shocks, receive integrated life-saving and life-sustaining assistance, and build resilience through services and alternative livelihood opportunities in Aleppo and Daraa. The objective of the project is two-fold: sustain the early recovery and resilience of target populations through short-term employment opportunities and vocational training (Outcome 1) and enhance the resilience of the most vulnerable populations through integrated protection services at community and individual levels (Outcome 2).ltbrgtCOOPI will implement the project in Aleppo (Al Khafsa in Manbij) and Daraa (Hrak, and Busra Esh-Sham) governorates. The proposed activities are informed by the findings of a recent field assessment carried out by COOPI staff in July 2024, and are in line with the sector priorities of the SHF allocation. The main findings confirmed the need for the enhancement of employability and entrepreneurship skills among target communities, empowering them to secure employment opportunities or start their own business. The lack of economic opportunities pushes families to resort to negative coping mechanisms, thus facing potential protection risks. The assessment, indeed, also identified the need for psychosocial support (PSS), group/individual counselling, and case management, targeting both vulnerable individuals and their caregiversltbrgtThe two project outcomes are expected to mutually reinforce each other. Specific selection criteria for each intervention have been developed to address specific vulnerabilities and enhance access and service inclusion. The deep contextual knowledge of COOPI as well as the acceptance of community and local authorities, and beneficiary consultations informed the design of activities.ltbrgtERL activities will foster early recovery and resilience through vocational and skills training, and job creation. Vocational and skills training will foster skills building and help individuals have better chances to be employed and start a small business. Furthermore, COOPI will provide in-kind assistance and regular coaching to new businesses set up by VT trainees and to existing businesses struggling due to the crisis. Special attention will be paid to the inclusion of businesses owned by women and people with disabilities.ltbrgtProtection activities, implemented in all four selected sub-districts will provide both community and individual specialized services (General, GBV, Child Protection and Mine Action) that help create a safer and more inclusive environment while preventing and responding to individual instances of violence. ERL beneficiaries will have increased awareness of protection risks and how to mitigate them, with specialized services available when necessary. COOPI will ensure the application of the do no harm principle during targeting and project implementation, in order to reduce tensions and foster social cohesion as much as possible.ltbrgtlt/pgt
